vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: agentads
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle (SKILL.md) provides instructions for an agent to subscribe to a 'Pay-per-Human' lead generation service, which involves high-risk financial and permission-granting activities. It directs the agent to add a specific third-party wallet address (0xb257b5c180b7b2cb80e35d6079abe68d9cf0467f) to its XMTP groups and pay USDC via an external x402-gated API (xmtp-agent-production-e08b.up.railway.app). While these actions are consistent with the stated purpose of the service, the hardcoded third-party control and financial commitment instructions represent a significant risk of unauthorized fund expenditure and group access if the agent follows them autonomously.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions mostly match its stated purpose, but there are noteworthy risks: it asks you to give an external address permission to add members to your group and to send payment/sensitive info through a third-party HTTP endpoint (railway.app/x402) with no provenance; verify the parties and test with small amounts before using.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (pay-per-human invites to an XMTP group) aligns with the SKILL.md steps: creating an XMTP group, adding Basemate's wallet, and subscribing. Required capabilities (XMTP identity, ERC-8004 registration, USDC balance) are consistent with the described flows. However, the skill references a non-official HTTP endpoint (a railway.app host) for programmatic subscriptions/payments which is not obviously part of XMTP/Base ecosystems and is worth verifying.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions direct you to create an XMTP group and explicitly add Basemate's wallet (0xb257...46f) with permission to add members. Granting that permission legitimately enables the service but also gives an external actor the ability to add people to your group — a material privilege. The programmatic path sends subscription data and payments to a third-party HTTP API (railway.app) and requires attaching x402 payment headers; this means your interests, group ID and payment actions are transmitted outside XMTP/Base. The skill does not instruct reading system files or env vars, but it does direct sharing of group identifiers and payments with that external host.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only (no install spec, no code files). That minimizes on-disk execution risk; there is no automatic package download or install described in the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request environment variables or secrets. It requires the agent to have an XMTP identity, ERC-8004 registration and USDC on Base — all proportional to a payment/growth service. No unrelated credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Flags show the skill is user-invocable and not always-on. The skill does require you to add an external wallet as a group member with add-permission, which is an application-level privilege (expected for the service), but the skill itself does not request persistent platform-level privileges or modification of other skills.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing or using this skill: 1) Verify the Basemate identity and wallet address out-of-band (do not trust only the SKILL.md text). 2) Understand that adding 0xb257...46f to your group with add-member permissions lets that external actor add people — consider the moderation and privacy implications and test in a throwaway group first. 3) The programmatic subscription/payment endpoint is hosted on railway.app (third-party); confirm the endpoint and x402 facilitator are legitimate and review their privacy/terms. 4) Start with a very small payment (or a test subscription) to confirm settlement behavior. 5) Keep a record of group IDs and any messages you send to the service; if anything unexpected happens, remove Basemate from the group and revoke permissions. 6) If you need higher assurance, ask the publisher for a homepage, code repository, or contract addresses for the payment facilitator and the on-chain settlement flow before proceeding.
